Regionally Significant Industrial Areas


Regionally Significant Industrial Areas

Established in 2011, the Regionally Significant Industrial Areas (RSIA) program designated areas planned and zoned for industrial use with the purpose of advancing job creation and economic development activities in Oregon. The program is no longer accepting nominations since the governing body which approved designations was dissolved in 2018.


A local government may adopt additional provisions that restrict the type or extent of current or future industrial uses within the area, as long as they mitigate the effect(s) of the new provision(s) by:
  • Clearly maintaining or increasing the industrial employment potential of the area; and
  • Clearly maintaining the important site characteristics and functions that led to the designation of the site.​

Local governments with land use authority over RSIAs must maintain the area for employment uses. The city or county may not:
  • Adopt a provision of a comprehensive plan or land use regulation that prevents industrial uses within the area;
  • Adopt a provision of a comprehensive plan or land use regulation that allows new non-industrial uses within the area that conflict with existing or planned industrial uses; or
  • Decrease the land area planned or zoned for industrial uses within the regionally significant industrial area.​

A Regionally Significant Industrial Area is an area planned and zoned for industrial use that:
  • Contains vacant sites, including brownfields, that are suitable for the location of new industrial uses or the expansion of existing industrial uses, and that collectively can provide significant additional employment in the region;
  • Has site characteristics that give the area significant competitive advantages that are difficult or impossible to replicate in the region;
  • Has superior access to transportation and freight infrastructure, including but not limited to rail, port, airport, multimodal freight or transshipment facilities, and other major transportation facilities or routes; and
  • Is located in close proximity to major labor markets.​

When an area is designated as a RSIA, all uses of the property that are allowed at the time of designation remain intact and are not limited. Changes in zoning and uses not currently allowed in the designated area are allowable, but the local government may not decrease the area of land planned and zoned for industrial use within the RSIA.

Designations remain in effect for at least 10 years. If 50 percent of the developable land within the designated area has not been developed within 10 years of the designation, the designation will be removed unless the majority of land owners within the area submit a formal request to Business Oregon. ​
